synopsis: The booklet draws on NIOSH for workplace-safety research, MSHA for mine accident records, and BLS data analyzed by CPWR for construction statistics; NIOSH has no enforcement power [f15654, f15655]. MSHA's calendar-2025 figures attribute 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%) and 426 of 4,792 nonfatal injuries (9%) to powered haulage [f3051, f3052]. Construction evidence includes 7,681 vehicle/mobile-equipment deaths during 1992–2010, about 404 annually, and 170 struck-by deaths in 2019, 47.1% involving transport vehicles [f3188, f3190, f3191]. NIOSH evidence exposes a research-coverage imbalance: vehicle-environment events represented 54% of 91 fatal haul-truck accidents reviewed for 2005–2018, while 85% of research cases addressed vehicle-vehicle interactions [f5821, f5824]. Alarm evidence needs reconciliation: the synthesis reports 18% false alarms and 42% nuisance alarms in a 2006 Caterpillar 793B study, whereas Chapter 7 reports 59% false or nuisance alarms in 2006–2007 [f102, f103, f5751]. Planning should account for databases' stronger coverage of fatalities than property damage or near misses, and must not combine different agencies' figures into one rate [f15671, f15672].
